subsenses.definition: A salesclerk; a person who serves customers in a store or market.
An employee at a hotel who deals with guests.
The chief legal advisor of a legislature or legislative chamber, who is usually also responsible for keeping minutes of sittings.

senses.definition: (Quakerism) A facilitator of a Quaker meeting for business affairs.
(archaic) In the Church of England, the layman that assists in the church service, especially in reading the responses (also called parish clerk and Bible clerk).

quotes.text: God save the King! Will no man say, amen? / Am I both priest and clerk? Well then, amen.

senses.definition: (dated) A cleric or clergyman (the legal title for clergy of the Church of England is "Clerk in Holy Orders", still used in legal documents and cherished by some of their number).

examples:
13th century, Traditional carol,
And all was for an appel, an appel that he toke/As clerkès finden written in their boke.

senses.definition: To act as a clerk, to perform the duties or functions of a clerk.
examples: The law school graduate clerked for the supreme court judge for the summer.
